configure.delta_caps_cases:
Short outage. Home Assistant was off for one night; the grid import meter increased by 12 kWh before the next poll. With the default 300 kWh grid cap, the full 12 kWh is applied once, attributed to the current Paris day and tariff slot (the integration does not reconstruct hour-by-hour consumption across the gap).

Very long outage or heavy catch-up. The same meter is 400 kWh higher when HA returns. A single delta of 400 exceeds the default 300 kWh grid cap: internal SSOT skips that chunk; logs / discard telemetry explain why. If your site often sees big jumps, raise the grid cap (for example 800–1500 kWh) or ensure HA stays up so deltas stay smaller.

PV inverter over-reporting for one tick. The solar kWh entity jumps by 30 kWh while actual production was tiny. A tighter solar cap (e.g. 40 kWh) caps how much of that spike can enter internal totals in one go; choose a value above the realistic maximum you expect between two hub polls under sunny conditions.

Large batteries or off-grid. Domestic lithium systems often move only a few kWh between updates; 80 kWh is already generous. A large stack cycling tens of kWh every few minutes might need a higher battery cap so legitimate fast ramps are not discarded.
configure.delta_caps_defaults:
Grid import & export — 300 kWh (shared cap for both)
Solar production — 120 kWh
Battery charge & discharge — 80 kWh per counter
Any other configured source — 200 kWh

Override all four values under Settings → Hub Énergie → Configure → Advanced: energy delta caps.
configure.delta_caps_ha: Shown only after install: Settings → Hub Énergie → Configure → Advanced — energy delta caps. Dialogs in Home Assistant may link here.
configure.delta_caps_intro: Hub Énergie compares each total_increasing meter reading to the last one it stored: the positive step is a delta. Within the cap for that source class (grid, solar, battery, other), kWh are booked into internal totals and the current tariff slot. Above the cap, the jump is treated as unrealistic: those kWh do not enter internal SSOT, but the stored raw reading still advances so the next delta is sane. Physical meters and Recorder stay the reference for raw totals; caps protect slot and cost math from spikes and huge catch-up after downtime.

scope.disclaimer: Behaviour depends on your hardware and entity selection (including the Energy dashboard). The lists above describe intended scope, not a guarantee for every edge case.
scope.exp_li1: Splitting battery charge origin by power flow when sensors are partial or noisy.
scope.exp_li2: Solar production estimation (model-based, not a physical meter).
scope.exp_li3: Opportunity-cost style diagnostics for exported kWh.
scope.stable_li1_d: Supplier (EDF vs custom), tariff modes (flat, HP–HC, multi-slot, EDF Tempo + RTE/API/sensor), grid, optional solar and batteries.
scope.stable_li2_d: Positive deltas from total_increasing meters → per-slot, per-day totals (Europe/Paris) and integration SSOT sensors.
scope.stable_li3_d: Daily € estimate, subscription split, per-slot detail in attributes.
scope.stable_li5_d: Grid-export split, data quality, delta telemetry, unknown bucket, staleness; health sensor with readable causes.
scope.stable_li6_d: Clear-sky PV estimate and solar resale when enabled.
